name: catalogue-page
title: Catalogue page
description: A shelf of things you make or sell, without a checkout: each item as a card with its photo, price and whether it's available, grouped by kind, with how to order, pickup or market hours, news and contact. For makers, market stalls, small bakeries and second-hand sellers.

images.purpose: each item's photo: a small square beside the item on phones, across the top of its card on wider screens. Give every item one; an item without one shows as a text card
images.alt_hint: what it is, its colour and size, e.g. A round sourdough loaf, dark crust, about 20 cm across
images.prompt: a real photo of the item on the same plain background as the others, in daylight, from the front, filling about 70% of the square

images.purpose: beside the headline on the home page: the stall, the shop window or a table of the goods; without it the headline and the ordering note sit side by side
images.prompt: a real photo of {subject}'s stall or table of goods, wide, in daylight

images.purpose: the round mark beside the name in the header (48 px) and the browser icon; must still read at 32 px
images.alt_hint: e.g. A wheat ear in a circle
images.prompt: a simple flat round emblem for {subject}, one shape, in the accent colour on the page's background colour, no words

images.purpose: the picture when a link is shared; empty uses the hero
a photo at the top of a news post's or market day's own page
images.prompt: a real photo of the new item or the market

content.purpose: the big headline, one line about what you make
how to order, in a dashed note under the headline, e.g. Message me to order; pick up Saturdays at the market. Say plainly there is no online checkout
the main button under the headline (with cta_link): e.g. Order by message (a tel:, mailto: or https link) or Buy on <your existing shop>; cta2_label and cta2_link make a second

the items, one card each, with a group (card.group) for each kind (Loaves, Pastries…): the cards_title heads the shelf, the group names make the jump links and the subheadings. On each card: name, description (short), price exactly as written, badge for availability (badge_tone live = available or new, building = sold out or limited), link + link_label for where to buy or ask (e.g. Buy on Etsy), tags for short labels (V, GF), subtitle for a size or weight. Confirm every price with the seller
the shelf's heading, e.g. This week's bakes
a list stream with events (market days: date, place, map link) shows them coming up first, then earlier; a list stream without events is news (new items, sold out, back soon) as dated rows
about the maker (about_title is its heading); the first paragraph prints larger
the closing block: phone, email, address (where to pick up or visit) with a directions link, social links; also in the footer
pickup, shop or market hours: open or closed now in the header and in the closing block with the weekly table, days off in the next 60 days, and a note (e.g. Orders by Thursday for Saturday pickup)
ways to order, as big buttons in the closing block, the first one filled: e.g. Text to order (tel:), Email an order (mailto:), Buy on our Etsy shop; note is the small line under each
a strip of tape across the top of every page for news that can't wait, e.g. Sold out of lemon loaves this week; with until it goes by itself
the footer line, e.g. the shop's name and where it is

art.ask: Ask for one clear photo of each item on a plain background in daylight, from the front, same background for all.
art.style: Real product photos, consistent background and crop; never invented or generated pictures of the goods. Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
steps: Collect one photo per item from your person, plus one of the stall or shop for the hero if they have it.
Check each item photo: square (crop to 1200x1200), sharp, the item fills about 70% of the frame, the same background and light as the others.
Write alt text for each: what it is, its colour and size.
Upload each one (an https link in its field, or photo_upload_link), then call theme_needs: every slot you used should say filled.
Confirm every price and every sold-out badge with the seller before publishing.
Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
